content: 1. Pharmacodynamic Synergism with Caffeine: The combination of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate with caffeine may theoretically increase the risk of bleeding due to the caffeine content. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Interaction with Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases the levels of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 3. Interaction with Heparin: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and heparin both increase anticoagulation, potentially enhancing each other's toxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 4. Interaction with Horse Chestnut Seed: Both aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and horse chestnut seed increase anticoagulation. Use caution and monitor the patient. 5. Interaction with Hyaluronidase: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of hyaluronidase. Salicylates in large systemic doses may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase, requiring larger amounts of the enzyme for equivalent dispersing effects. Use caution and monitor. 6. Interaction with Hydralazine: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of hydralazine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Interaction with Hydrochlorothiazide: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium, while hydrochlorothiazide decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 8. Interaction with Hydrocortisone: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and hydrocortisone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor. 9. Interaction with Ibuprofen: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and ibuprofen both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium. Additionally, aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may increase the levels or effects of intravenous ibuprofen by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 10. Interaction with Icosapent: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and icosapent may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Icosapent may prolong bleeding time, necessitating periodic monitoring when co-administered with other drugs affecting bleeding. Use caution and monitor. 11. Interaction with Indapamide: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium, while indapamide decreases it. The overall effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 12. Interaction with Indomethacin: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and indomethacin both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 13. Interaction with Irbesartan: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of irbesartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs increase serum potassium, and their combination may result in renal function deterioration, particularly in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 14. Interaction with Isoproterenol: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium, while isoproterenol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 15. Interaction with Ketoprofen: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and ketoprofen both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 16. Interaction with Ketorolac: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and ketorolac (including intranasal formulations) both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 17. Interaction with Labetalol: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of labetalol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs increase serum potassium. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may exacerbate this interaction. Use caution and monitor. 18. Interaction with Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of ledipasvir by increasing gastric pH, as ledipasvir solubility decreases with higher pH. Separate the administration of antacids and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by at least 4 hours. Use caution and monitor. 19. Interaction with Levalbuterol: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium, while levalbuterol decreases it. The overall effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 20. Interaction with Levomilnacipran: Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and levomilnacipran may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. SNRIs like levomilnacipran may further impair platelet activity in patients taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs. Use caution and monitor.
